correctness.rationale: Every length-three word has at most three distinct length-two deletion descendants, giving the lower bound ceil(q^2/3). For q congruent 3 mod 6, q>=9, choose the cycle C_q as a partial-triple-system leave; for q congruent 1 or 5 mod 6 choose C_{q-1} plus one isolated vertex. The Colbourn–Rosa theorem applies because all leave degrees are zero or two, the necessary parity/divisibility conditions hold, and the lone exception C4 union C5 is never selected. Two opposite words per triangle cover all six orientations of its three edges; one word (v_i,v_{i+1},v_i) per cycle edge covers both orientations plus loop (v_i,v_i), and the isolated symbol uses (z,z,z). The counts simplify to ceil(q^2/3). q=3 is covered by the explicit three-word cycle code. Fresh independent checks reproduce complete coverage and exact size for q=5,7,9,11,13.

evidence: Colbourn–Rosa classify a broad class of leaves for maximal partial triple systems.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither broader result alone gives the exact coding-theoretic formula; the audit combines the counting lower bound with a specific leave choice and orientation/loop completion.
